code: The percentage-brightness helper chooses the smallest array dimension as bands. A (7,2,3) band-first cube is moved so its two image rows become the apparent bands.
expected: Each known band should receive its own coefficient, independent of image size.
difference: Array shape is used as a proxy for the semantic band axis.
outputs: Yes. Gains can be applied across rows and only two coefficients used. The small fixture reproduces this.
existing_results: Impact not yet established. Trace actual product shapes and the generating code path.
action: Use an explicit band-axis contract, test both layouts and edge shapes, then audit affected product provenance.

code: Chunk starts and ends use integer row conversion with an extra end row. Consecutive windows overlap; the 3×3 fixture emits 15 rows for nine pixels.
expected: Each selected raster/pixel identity should occur once.
difference: Flat chunk boundaries are converted to whole-row windows without trimming duplicated rows.
outputs: Yes. Counts and downstream summaries can change; weighting duplicated pixels may alter medians.
existing_results: Impact not yet established. Determine whether the historical library used this extractor and whether duplicates were removed.
action: Use disjoint row blocks or trimmed flat windows, assert unique source/pixel keys, quantify impacts before creating new versioned outputs.

code: Inline convolution divides by response sum plus 10⁻¹². Zero support produces zero; negative weights are not rejected.
expected: An exact normalized nonnegative average preserves constants and bounds.
difference: The stabilizing denominator changes the normalization; the exact-real factor is sum/(sum+epsilon).
outputs: Yes, strongly when support is tiny. Ordinary well-supported bands may have negligible differences.
existing_results: Impact not yet established; the near-zero toy is not a measured production-band error.
severity: Low for ordinary support; high for near-zero support.
action: Validate response sign/support and choose an explicit zero-support policy; retain the epsilon-specific theorem until implementation changes.

code: SCS+C fits coefficients; BRDF can choose NDVI bins; scene brightness fits parameters and usually clips.
expected: A linear theorem requires one fixed operator on common support.
difference: Re-estimation, bin selection and clipping can change the operator with its input.
outputs: Yes if an analyst reorders operations or assumes full-pipeline linearity. This is not itself an implementation bug.
existing_results: Impact not yet established for any improper reorder; the existing ordering is preserved.
action: State frozen-parameter hypotheses and retain the documented correction order.

finding: A5 | MESMA is a restricted numerical search
code: The code limits categories/models, excludes tiny interiors, skips numerically weak Gram systems and updates only beyond a 10⁻¹⁴ MSE improvement.
expected: An unrestricted exact argmin ranges over every mathematically allowed candidate.
difference: The executed search admits only a finite, thresholded subset and uses a tie tolerance.
outputs: Yes relative to an unrestricted ideal solver, particularly near boundaries or degeneracy.
existing_results: Impact not yet established beyond documented solver controls; exact-real optimality is not asserted for Python.
severity: Specification boundary, not automatically a bug.
action: Use the admitted-search tolerance theorem; retain rank/interior/tie settings and avoid unrestricted-optimum claims.

finding: A6 | Ambiguity is not exhaustive uncertainty
code: One best fraction solution is stored per class set; near-fit ranges use those solutions within chosen RMSE + 0.01.
expected: All feasible near-optimal fractions would define a larger uncertainty question.
difference: The saved diagnostic samples candidate-class-set winners, not every feasible composition.
outputs: It changes which alternatives are represented; it need not change the selected estimate.
existing_results: The existing diagnostic is not an exhaustive physical interval. Broader field impact is not established.
action: Name the retained library, metric, tolerance and restricted range; do not call it full physical uncertainty.

code: Ridge uses proper-training standardization, fit_intercept=True and calibration-selected alpha.
expected: The inverse formula must use centered transformed design/targets and restore the unpenalized intercept.
difference: A naive uncentered formula describes a different model.
outputs: Yes if the wrong formula is used for replay or explanation; the audited implementation uses the stated conventions.
existing_results: No leakage was found in inspected preprocessing code; this is inspection/numerical evidence, not a workflow proof.
action: Keep means, scales, centering, alpha and intercept in replay provenance; use the proved centered objective.

finding: A8 | Library medians are not means
code: Extraction emits pixels; the primary library aggregates hierarchical medians with unsupported bands missing.
expected: The mean commutation theorem applies to normalized arithmetic averaging on fixed support.
difference: Medians are nonlinear under arbitrary addition/cross-band mixing.
outputs: Yes if a mean theorem is used to reorder median aggregation and transformation.
existing_results: Impact not yet established for any altered order; no aggregation was changed.
action: Describe actual medians and common support; use the proved median counterexample rather than a mean claim.

code: Inline Gaussian sampling, input-width-weighted legacy fallback and optional HyTools implementations differ; the legacy wrapper assumes 426 bands/FWHM5.
expected: A coefficient-equivalence claim would require the same actual coefficient construction.
difference: Backends and defaults encode different approximations and metadata assumptions.
outputs: Yes. Frozen matrices can all be linear while producing different numbers.
existing_results: Impact not yet established across historical backends.
action: Record backend/version/input metadata, pin optional dependencies and do not claim universal coefficient equivalence.

finding: A10 | Synthetic coefficients are not independent calibration
code: The packaged drone registry was fitted between synthetic products from corrected NEON; range checks guard numerical compatibility.
expected: Physical calibration transfer requires independent aligned native-sensor observations.
difference: A complete synthetic fit or high correlation does not establish empirical cross-sensor validity.
outputs: Applied coefficients change outputs; physical correctness is not established by their algebra.
existing_results: Native-drone/actual-Landsat validity remains an empirical question.
action: Collect independent calibration/validation observations; retain diagnostic provenance and explicit sensor direction.

finding: A11 | Missing data change the domain
code: Inline products reset all-band nodata pixels; partial nodata/NaNs can enter sums. Extraction rejects -9999 but not every nonfinite value.
expected: Real-vector theorems require finite common support and aligned masks.
difference: Array missingness is not represented by a finite real number; masks can alter effective operators.
outputs: Yes. Invalid values can propagate or contaminate weighted values.
existing_results: Impact not yet established; quantify actual partial-missing cases before judging a dataset.
action: Declare and test per-band support and nodata policies; preserve legitimate finite negative corrected values.

code: The scene-brightness helper treats the array as band-first when its first dimension is no larger than its last.
expected: Accepted layouts need a known band axis.
difference: A relative-size comparison cannot identify semantics for every shape.
outputs: Yes for ambiguous shapes; fitting and clipping can compound interpretation differences.
existing_results: Impact not yet established; this finding is confirmed by inspection, not the separate A1 fixture.
action: Add an explicit axis contract and layout tests; do not treat default clipping as globally affine.

code: The helper accesses pyarrow.parquet without explicitly importing that submodule. A fresh isolated run raised AttributeError.
expected: The advertised extraction path should initialize its own dependency.
difference: Execution can depend on whether another import has already loaded the submodule.
outputs: It can prevent execution; it does not silently change a successfully produced spectrum.
existing_results: Impact not yet established. The overlap fixture imports the submodule explicitly to reach the loop.
action: Import pyarrow.parquet inside the lazy helper and test a fresh process.

code: Decimal centers/FWHM enter inline construction as float32; polygon wavelength labels are rounded to integer nm.
expected: Response construction should use authoritative response metadata.
difference: A rounded column name omits decimal-center precision and the response width/function.
outputs: Reconstructing an operator from labels alone can change results; ordinary labeling does not change prior convolution values.
existing_results: Impact not yet established for any metadata reconstruction. No coefficient-direction error was found in the inspected application.
action: Use original header/configuration responses, preserve their hashes and distinguish labels from sensor definitions.
